axis: Sparse FFN beyond MoE routing: trained-in activation sparsity (ReLU-fication/ProSparse-class), predictor-based sparsity (LLM-in-a-Flash class), and contextual sparsity (Deja Vu/PowerInfer lineage)
summary: This axis is the mirror image of the DSpark/DFlash case: the science is real but the runtime-observable surface that made AXI-SA cheap does not exist here on the primary instrument. Speculation earned first-class counters because MLX-native ports (e.g. ARahim3/mlx-dspark, per the web memo) emit per-round proposed/accepted signals; nothing in the repo, the vendored clone (zero sparsity mentions), or the memo grounds ANY Apple-Silicon runtime that actually skips FFN compute from activation sparsity — a ReLU-fied checkpoint on MLX runs dense, so on the Mac the axis is energy-invisible by construction (that null is itself a reportable row). The exercisable leg, if any, is the 3080 Ti: the PowerInfer lineage targets consumer NVIDIA GPUs with ReLU-fied checkpoints, but current 30-series/12 GiB support and artifact availability are NEEDS-WEB, and Deja Vu's artifact is A100-class research code (NEEDS-WEB). On reduction: the whole-request contrast reduces cleanly to existing patterns — C5-1.8's stack-conditioned runtime attribution (sparse runtime vs dense runtime differ in more than sparsity) and C5-1.12's model-surgery divergence discipline (ReLU-fied model is not the base model); what is genuinely new is only the dynamic-active-parameter question — whether energy tracks a per-request activated-parameter fraction, turning C5-1.1's static active-parameter coefficient input-dependent under the Q4 thesis — and that question is gated on a runtime counter no fleet runtime is grounded to expose. Identifiability is therefore the binding constraint: sparsity leaves token streams untouched (same tokens, same counts, no decode_emission analogue), so the harness sees only the whole-request energy shadow unless a self-reported, harness-unverifiable runtime counter appears. Process note: a Sol high read-only scout was launched via the audited codex-run-v3 path per the skill, but the workflow deadline landed before its envelope returned; per protocol a missing envelope is never treated as a result, so this evaluation is lead-grounded in the named repo files and the web memo, with all ungrounded runtime claims marked NEEDS-WEB. Net: a thin 3080 Ti-leg contrast and one likely-null Mac row are cheap and honest; a first-class sparsity axis is not currently buildable to AXI-SA standard.
harness_difficulty: Already covered (bench-scale): a whole-request gross-energy contrast between a sparse-capable runtime and a dense baseline needs NO new schema — gross_energy_j on gross_request (docs/contracts/token_normalization.md Primary Metric), with the sparse runtime carried in the existing stack-identity table rows (Runtime+version, Kernel/library where known; token_normalization.md §Stack-Identity Table) and metadata.runtime/metadata.adapters.runtime. That is the C5-1.8 shape verbatim. NOT covered (multi-session to new-subsystem): a first-class sparsity axis analogous to speculation. The landed AXI-SA contract (docs/specs/axi/sa_burst_decode_contract.md §2.1) makes extensions scoped and fail-closed — unknown schema_extensions names fail validation — so a SparsityPolicy would need a NEW scoped extension (joulewise.axi_sparsity_config.v2-style) beside joulewise.axi_decode_config.v1 in joulewise/axi_decode_config.py; per-step activated-parameter counters would need a new event surface, since validate_v2_event enforces exact-key metadata (EMISSION_KEYS are speculation-specific: tokens_proposed/tokens_accepted have no sparsity analogue) and forbids leaked fields; plus reducer additions (SUMMARY_REDUCER_VERSION bump path, §8), registry rows, and C-023-style identity gates. That mirrors the entire AXI-SA arc — and unlike AXI-SA it is blocked upstream on a runtime signal that is not grounded to exist, and any such counter would be runtime-self-reported with no harness-side cross-check (speculation's counters are validated by the token-partition rule emitted = accepted + target; sparsity has no equivalent conservation law visible in tokens).
feasibility: Mac/MLX today: NOT exercisable as sparsity. No sparse-FFN execution path is grounded in MLX/mlx-lm; the vendored /Users/edr/code/mlx-dspark-vendor is speculative decoding only (grep for spars* returns nothing), and the web memo (scratchpad/dflash-dspark-web.md) covers only DFlash/DSpark. A ReLU-fied checkpoint would execute densely on MLX — weights differ, compute does not skip — so only the C5-SF.3 null-shaped row is honestly runnable on the Mac. Whether any community MLX kernel exploits activation sparsity: NEEDS-WEB. 3080 Ti (12 GiB, CUDA; D-073 fleet): the plausible leg — the PowerInfer lineage (contextual sparsity, neuron-placement across CPU/GPU) historically targets consumer NVIDIA GPUs and ReLU-fied models (ProSparse/TurboSparse-class checkpoints), which would fit 12 GiB at 7B-class quantized; current PowerInfer support for a 30-series card, build health, and checkpoint availability are all NEEDS-WEB. Deja Vu itself is A100-class research code, not a deployable runtime (NEEDS-WEB for any maintained fork). llama.cpp (both legs): no activation-sparsity compute-skipping path grounded anywhere in repo evidence — NEEDS-WEB. AMD/other: out of fleet per D-073 (Mac + 3080 Ti primary; Jetson optional replication only) — not evaluated.

risks: (1) Primary-instrument blindness: the axis is energy-invisible on the Mac/MLX leg absent a sparse kernel, so the flagship quiet-Mac instrument contributes only a null row — poor return on [QUIET-MAC] hardware time that D-070 already commits to five axes. (2) Runtime confound is structural, not incidental: every exercisable contrast is sparse-runtime-vs-dense-runtime, capped at C5-1.8-style stack-conditioned language forever unless a single runtime gains a sparsity on/off switch (NEEDS-WEB). axis: KV-cache management (paged / quantized / evicting caches) + unified flat KV memory pool concept
summary: This axis splits cleanly into a measurable core and a speculative shell. The core — quantized-KV decode energy and evicting/rotating-window energy — is measurable on the Mac TODAY with zero runtime work: installed mlx-lm 0.31.3 (repo .venv) exposes kv_bits/kv_group_size/quantized_kv_start and max_kv_size directly on the generate path (generate.py:299-345, maybe_quantize_kv_cache), backed by QuantizedKVCache (cache.py:232), RotatingKVCache (cache.py:410, selected by make_prompt_cache max_kv_size at cache.py:15-37), ChunkedKVCache, BatchKVCache, plus save/load/trim_prompt_cache (cache.py:43-113) and an LRUPromptCache/PromptTrie layer (cache.py:1532-1623) for cache-persistence economics. Critically, these on-device questions are NOT what the existing rows bank: C5-2.3 (bank:839) and C5-2.4 (bank:848) are both transfer-leg questions gated on P1-004/P1-006 links, so an on-device KV-policy axis un-gates the quantization question and makes it runnable now on the D-073 fleet. The 'paged' leg is different: installed mlx-lm has NO paged/block-table cache class (the inventory is concatenate- and step-growing-buffer styles), so paged KV means either a new runtime adapter (vLLM on the 3080 Ti, NEEDS-WEB for 12 GiB feasibility) or runtime modification — not harness glue. The flat-pool concept is mostly systems-research speculation with weak energy coupling: MLX already runs a unified-memory allocator whose observables are exposed (mx.get_active_memory/get_cache_memory/get_peak_memory/set_cache_limit, verified importable in the repo venv), so an investigation could only measure allocator counters under cache-policy contrasts and try to correlate them with energy; the vendored mlx-dspark clone even records a measured null on exactly this kind of allocator contrast (model.py:53: preallocated KVCache-style buffer vs plain concatenate = 0.99x at <=600 tokens). Framed per D-070, the measurable core is a clean Q4 stress test — cache policy should move the marginal (bandwidth-bound) coefficient while leaving the fixed term alone — which is the strongest reason to admit it.
harness_difficulty: Verified by grep: the string "cache" appears ZERO times in all three landed AXI-SA surfaces — docs/contracts/token_normalization.md, joulewise/axi_decode_config.py, joulewise/schemas.py — so cache-config identity is genuinely new surface. What is reusable: the request-scoped event schema and lifecycle envelopes (D-070 clause 3), the burst/decode counter keys (axi_decode_config.py:423-429: tokens_proposed/tokens_accepted/target_emitted_count/emitted_token_ids), and the identity-block pattern — SpeculationPolicy (axi_decode_config.py:216) and BatchPolicy (:253) are the exact template for a new CachePolicy block (cache_class, kv_bits, kv_group_size, quantized_kv_start, max_kv_size/keep, persistence on/off). The token_normalization.md Stack-Identity Table (§ at line 114) has a Quantization field (weight quant) and a Batching/concurrency field but no KV-cache-policy field — a one-row contract amendment. Rough sizes: quantized-KV and rotating-window contrasts = single-session (kwarg pass-through in the MLX adapter + CachePolicy identity + stack-identity row); prompt-cache save/load/replay energy = bench-to-single-session (RQ-MLX-KV-REPLAY already answered the L1 feasibility leg, registry:61); per-step memory telemetry channel (sampling mx.get_peak_memory into the bundle) = single-session additive; paged KV via a new vLLM adapter = new-subsystem; flat-pool with runtime modification = new-subsystem and post-capstone shaped.
feasibility: Mac/MLX today: YES for the core. Installed mlx-lm 0.31.3 at .venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/mlx_lm — quantized KV via kv_bits/kv_group_size/quantized_kv_start (generate.py:299-345), evicting window via max_kv_size -> RotatingKVCache(keep=4) (models/cache.py:15-37, 410), persistence via save/load/trim_prompt_cache (cache.py:43-113), LRU prompt cache (cache.py:1623); allocator observables via mx.get_active_memory/get_cache_memory/get_peak_memory/set_cache_limit (verified importable in repo venv). Paged/block-table KV: ABSENT from installed mlx-lm — no such class exists in cache.py; whether upstream MLX has paged attention planned is NEEDS-WEB. 3080 Ti (D-073 primary, 12 GiB): C5-2.4 (bank:848) already presumes llama.cpp q8_0 cache support and gates on a cache-portability spike verdict; exact llama.cpp cache-type flags/coverage and any llama.cpp paged-KV status are NEEDS-WEB (not grounded in repo files). vLLM on 3080 Ti would provide true PagedAttention block tables but is a whole new runtime adapter and its 12 GiB fit for the D-074 Qwen3-4B primary is NEEDS-WEB. AMD/other: outside the D-073 fleet (Mac + 3080 Ti primary; Jetson optional, non-cap-setting replication only). The web memo (dflash-dspark-web.md) is spec-decode-focused and adds only adjacent evidence here: the vendored mlx-dspark clone rolls back the target KV cache after rejected drafts (generate.py:576,986) and documents a measured prealloc-vs-concatenate allocator null (model.py:53), which bears directly on the flat-pool leg's expected effect size.

(2) Cadence: per-token attribution is invalid — RQ-KV-GROWTH's registry row (registry:48) already bans per-token joule claims because token cadence outruns power sampling; every row above must inherit chunked-window discipline. (3) Unified-memory confound: MLX's lazy evaluation and Metal buffer cache mean footprint deltas do not map linearly to DRAM-traffic (hence energy) deltas; set_cache_limit state must be pinned in config identity or runs are incomparable. (5) Scope creep: the paged leg tempts a vLLM adapter (new subsystem) for one row; the flat-pool leg tempts runtime engineering with an expected near-null effect (mlx-dspark model.py:53). axis: Unified kernel APIs / shared scheduler-runtime logic across NVIDIA and AMD (portable kernel layers, shared serving runtimes)
summary: The literal NVIDIA-vs-AMD question is out of reach for this capstone: the D-073 fleet is a 128 GB M3 Max plus a 3080 Ti (12 GiB), Jetson optional replication only, and no AMD hardware exists or is planned; D-070 caps every axis at L2 as a stress test of the single Q4 thesis. The honest within-fleet reductions of this axis already have registry homes: C5-2.7 is exactly "same llama.cpp build/model/quant across devices with the runtime variable removed" (the portable-kernel-runtime-as-controlled-variable design, bank line ~865), C5-1.8 is same-machine cross-runtime energy attribution (bank line ~668), and C5-3.3 already holds the cross-ISA/AMD platform question as hardware-gated L4-after-replication. What the axis genuinely adds is not a new askable question but an explanatory variable: kernel-layer identity (attention kernel, BLAS/GEMM backend, Triton-vs-handwritten, graph/capture mode), which today is only best-effort adapter metadata ("Kernel/library where known" row of the stack-identity table maps to metadata.adapters.runtime.prepare_metadata "when captured"). Both within-reach designs are partially confounded — the Metal-vs-CUDA llama.cpp comparison carries a device+measurement-boundary confound (powermetrics SoC rails vs nvidia-smi board power; per-boundary claims only until wall-calibrated per C5-2.9), and the same-silicon 3080 Ti cross-runtime comparison is stack-vs-stack when artifact formats differ, exactly as C5-1.8's methodology note already caps it. Verdict: this is predominantly a post-capstone platform question; the capstone-reach content is (a) a cheap kernel-provenance rider on C5-2.7/C5-1.8 and (b) minimal backend-provenance fields so bundles recorded now stay comparable if an AMD/ROCm leg arrives later under C5-3.3. A Sol high-effort read-only confirmation session was still in flight at the reporting deadline (audit trail: /Users/edr/code/JouleWise/.codex-bridge/20260717T071715Z-83677-new.*, session 019f6eef-c802-78a3-9629-c44baaf4c293); all repo claims here are lead-verified directly against the files cited.
harness_difficulty: Already covered: joulewise/schemas.py defines closed-set RuntimeBackend {mock, mlx, vllm, llama_cpp, hailo} and TelemetryBackend {mock, powermetrics, nvidia_smi, jetson_rails, wall_meter} (lines ~180-193) with hardware_target requiring both (line ~399); the AXI-SA contract already makes runtime identity first-class per drafter — DraftModelIdentity carries runtime_backend + runtime_version (joulewise/axi_decode_config.py lines ~144-172) — and metadata.runtime carries primary_source_identity, target_model_artifact_sha256, target_tokenizer_identity (axi_decode_config.py ~658-663); docs/contracts/token_normalization.md's stack-identity table mandates a "Kernel/library where known" field but routes it to metadata.adapters.runtime.prepare_metadata "when captured" (see docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md ~706-715) — i.e. optional adapter metadata, not validated schema. New surface needed: (1) a named additive kernel-library identity block (name/version/provenance for flash-attn or equivalent attention kernel, Triton, cuBLAS/Metal-MPS/MLX-fast-kernels, plus backend build target CUDA/Metal/HIP) under metadata.runtime or a validated adapters field — session-scale; (2) RuntimeBackend enum extensions (sglang, tensorrt_llm; someday a ROCm-backed value) — bench-scale and purely additive since the enum is closed-set at validation time, so old bundles are unaffected; (3) TelemetryBackend has no AMD value (rocm-smi) — an AMD leg is a new-subsystem (new telemetry adapter, exactly what C5-3.3 names as its deliverable); (4) scheduler identity for shared serving runtimes needs no new event schema — D-070 clause 3 already pinned request-scoped events (metadata.request_id) precisely so continuous-batching/scheduler work stays additive. Sizing: provenance fields = one session; enum additions = bench; a cross-backend measurement campaign = multi-session (quiet-Mac + 3080 Ti windows); AMD leg = new-subsystem, post-capstone.
feasibility: Mac/MLX today: llama.cpp-Metal and MLX both run on the M3 Max under powermetrics (RuntimeBackend.MLX/LLAMA_CPP and TelemetryBackend.POWERMETRICS already exist in joulewise/schemas.py); MLX-side burst-decode is live via the vendored ARahim3/mlx-dspark clone (/Users/edr/code/mlx-dspark-vendor, per the web memo). 3080 Ti: llama.cpp-CUDA and vLLM are the plausible legs under nvidia_smi telemetry at the 12 GiB cap (D-073); DFlash-on-vLLM comes via the speculators project flagged "under active development, not all hardware validated" (web memo, speculators doc), and TensorRT-LLM DFlash recipes are published for Blackwell/Hopper — Ampere (3080 Ti) support is NEEDS-WEB; TensorRT-LLM and SGLang are also absent from the RuntimeBackend enum today. axis: DSpark + DFlash as measurable speculative-decoding methods (MLX-first via vendored mlx-dspark; DFlash-via-speculators on the vLLM/NVIDIA leg)
summary: Both methods are lossless draft-then-verify with a SEPARATE drafter artifact, and the landed AXI-SA model fits their per-round semantics without schema change: decode_emission records per-round OBSERVED tokens_proposed/tokens_accepted with emitted_count = accepted + target bonus, so DSpark's variable-K confidence scheduling is naturally representable (per-event proposed counts vary under the fixed max_proposed_tokens cap, which is a cap, not an assumed K) and DFlash's fixed K=8/16 is the trivial case. Both bucket as speculation mode "draft_model" with DraftModelIdentity (own sha/quant/tokenizer fields fit the mlx-dspark drafter checkpoints); native_mtp remains the structural contrast (no separate drafter forward, so only DSpark/DFlash admit a drafter-vs-target energy story at all). Two real gaps: the exact-keyed emission schema has no proposal-ORIGIN field, so mlx-dspark's hybrid n-gram lookup (on by default even inside dspark mode) must be pinned off via --no-lookup-drafts and verified via GenResult.lookup_rounds == 0, since per-round origin tagging would need a contract successor; and an in-round drafter-vs-target energy split is neither claimable as an additive decomposition (contract §7.2 non-additive rule, §8.4 attribution boundary) nor physically resolvable at powermetrics cadence over millisecond rounds — the honest design is spec-on/off ablation plus a drafter-only microbenchmark. Lead-verified in the vendored clone: GenResult already exposes per-round accept_lengths, target_forwards, and lookup_rounds today; only per-round PROPOSED counts need a thin instrumentation shim. The MLX leg is measurable now in a dedicated venv (mlx>=0.32.0 required vs harness pin mlx 0.31.2); the 3080 Ti leg is DFlash-via-vLLM-speculators with Ampere validation NEEDS-WEB and DSpark mainline vLLM UNCONFIRMED. (7) Continuous batching (--max-batch) and the server's prefix cache are contract-forbidden/confounding conveniences that the adapter must disable. (8) Attribution physics: any per-round drafter-vs-verify joules split is unresolvable at powermetrics cadence on one SoC rail and forbidden as an additive decomposition by §7.2 — claims must stay ablation-shaped. candidate_rows.forbidden_upgrade: No efficiency claim without exact output identity (C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY), runtime-observed loaded MTP heads, and accepted/proposed accounting per token_normalization.md; committed-burst length is never the accepted-token denominator.

What is missing is entirely runtime-side: (1) an MLX decode primitive that actually executes MTP heads with per-round counters — new-subsystem scale on the Mac today since pinned mlx-lm strips the heads (drops to one-session adapter work only if an upstream primitive appears); (2) a live adapter emitting AxiDecodeEmission/AxiRuntimeResult for the mechanism — session-scale on CUDA if vLLM exposes hooks (NEEDS-WEB); (3) runtime-observed head provenance (loaded MTP tensor inventory validated against NativeMTPIdentity) — currently the adapter could assert native_mtp over a stripped artifact and pass validation, a real gap Sol identified; (4) a frozen candidate-position counting rule for head/depth/tree topologies (head_count, draft_depth, head_configuration are currently opaque positives). Embarrassment modes: adapter asserts native_mtp identity over a stripped artifact and passes validation (no runtime-observed head provenance yet); H x D or committed-burst length mistaken for the proposed/accepted denominators — including the vendored mlx-dspark trap where public accept_lengths stores committed (accepted+bonus) tokens (Sol's unique catch: x_mlx_dspark is NOT valid C5-2.5 accounting as-is); DSpark conflated with native MTP because both are DeepSeek-associated (DSpark is a separate semi-autoregressive drafter, mode=draft_model under the contract's artifact-locus rule); 'no separate drafter' promoted to 'no extra residency/compute'; mechanism results pooled across DSpark/DFlash/MTP despite the one-mechanism-per-registry rule; Mac results generalized to the 3080 Ti despite disjoint model fits. summary: Native MTP is the best-covered and least-runnable of the burst-decode mechanisms: the landed AXI-SA contract already treats it as a first-class speculation mode with its own identity object, registry IDs, family, fixtures, and identical counter semantics to external-draft, so essentially zero new contract surface is needed — but no reachable runtime executes MTP heads today. The decisive grounded fact (which Sol flagged NEEDS-WEB and I resolved at the bench): pinned mlx-lm 0.31.3 in the repo venv strips MTP weights at model load for every MTP-bearing architecture it ships (qwen3_next, mimo, mimo_v2_flash), while fully supporting external-draft speculation — so the Mac leg's characterized burst-decode claims should route to DSpark/DFlash now, with native MTP held as a gated feasibility row. The scientific case for keeping it is real and Q4-shaped: self-drafting removes the external drafter's residency and forwards, making the drafter's fixed-cost term the experimental variable — the cleanest mechanism-level stress of E = fixed + coefficients*work in the whole speculation axis. The C5-2.5 denominator story survives intact under native MTP (proposed = realized candidate positions submitted to verification, never head_count x draft_depth; accepted excludes the bonus token; J/accepted-token stays a spec-on-only mechanism-yield diagnostic with no drafter-energy attribution possible or claimed), with one naming caution: report language should say 'accepted proposal (draft/MTP) token'. Fleet-wise, MiMo-7B is the only named candidate plausibly spanning both legs (model knowledge, unverified); the 12 GiB CUDA cap eliminates DeepSeek-V3/Qwen3-Next/GLM-class. Ranking for the Mac leg: DSpark first, DFlash second, native MTP third as a four-gate spike (heads in source weights, retained through conversion, executed with round counters, exact-output on/off smoke). Enrichment is medium: high distinctness but low near-term askability, and the in-flight AXI-SC spike will supply the authoritative mlx-lm verdict either way.

axis: Transformer architecture variants (dense vs MoE vs hybrid/SSM-mixers) and attention mechanisms (GQA vs MLA vs sliding-window vs sparse) as energy-profile subjects, including whether attention-vs-FFN phase attribution is in scope of the current event model
summary: Sol's read-only high-effort assessment (bridge run 20260717T071639Z-74891, OK, valid envelope; lead checks replayed) splits this axis in two. The hybrid/SSM-mixer half is the valuable part: it stresses whether Q4's work coefficients survive when context-growing attention is replaced by recurrent state — a genuinely different stress than the already-committed MoE axis (conditional FFN activation, D-070) — and near-runnable subjects exist (Granite 4.0 H-Micro 3B vs Micro 3B as a named same-family hybrid/transformer pair; the state-spaces transformerpp/mamba2attn/mamba2 2.7B trio trained on the same 300B Pile tokens as the scientifically strongest but runtime-unverified design; Qwen3.5-4B DeltaNet-hybrid vs the already-mirrored Qwen3-4B GQA as a stack-generation contrast). The attention-mechanism half is currently weak: no MLA/GQA or SWA/full pair survives single-axis scrutiny (DeepSeek-V2-Lite MLA is confounded with MoE/size/tokenizer; Gemma generations change everything at once), llama.cpp's --swa-full is a cache-allocation toggle not an attention toggle, and --flash-attn is a kernel A/B not a mechanism A/B; sparse attention has no verified local execution path (Phi-3-small's block-sparse kernels are Triton/CUDA, NEEDS-WEB whether they actually execute on the fleet). On attribution: attention-vs-FFN time-slicing is OUT of scope of the landed event model — AXI-SA phases are request-lifecycle-level (phase_start/phase_end with request_phase_ordinal), powermetrics cadence cannot resolve per-layer intervals, and the RQ-SHORT-PREFILL-RESOLVABILITY precedent already rules out sub-cadence joule claims — so the honest designs are whole-request contrasts (nothing new needed) and fixed-output decode-phase context-length regressions whose context-associated slope must never be renamed an "attention energy fraction". Enrichment verdict medium overall: medium-high for the mixer sub-axis, low-medium marginal for attention mechanisms today since C5-1.2/RQ-KV-GROWTH already carry the context/KV-scaling question.
harness_difficulty: Landed and sufficient for whole-request contrasts: gross_request/gross_batch_group window classes, events v2 with request-scoped phases and decode_emission (docs/specs/axi/sa_burst_decode_contract.md §§1-4), reducer 0.6.0, model/quant/artifact identity in ModelConfig (joulewise/schemas.py:349) plus MLX adapter runtime capture (joulewise/adapters/mlx_runtime.py:148), and — importantly — the stack-identity table already reserves 'Kernel/library where known: attention implementation' (docs/contracts/token_normalization.md:132), so attention-mechanism identity has a contractual home. The joulewise.axi_decode_config.v1 extension (joulewise/axi_decode_config.py) covers only batch_policy and speculation — it carries no architecture-taxonomy fields, and unknown config keys do not enter normalized identity (schemas.py extension handling), so an auditable architecture manifest (mechanism, layer pattern, Q/KV heads, trained window, SSM type, source-config digest) is new surface: bench-size if kept as campaign-side selection evidence, session-size if promoted into normalized metadata. Context-sweep regression designs are session-size and largely reuse C5-1.2/RQ-KV-GROWTH machinery plus an analysis plan. A matched-quant conversion + S-D-style G1-G10 receipts for a hybrid pair is session-size. Attention-vs-FFN module attribution is NOT in scope of the current event model: request-level phases cannot be relabeled module phases, and adding per-layer markers would not create power samples at per-layer timescales (powermetrics cadence; RQ-SHORT-PREFILL-RESOLVABILITY precedent, docs/research_question_registry.md:60) — module-isolating synthetic microbenchmarks or per-layer instrumentation are each a new subsystem, and the latter may remain unsuitable even after instrumentation. A llama.cpp adapter for the 3080 Ti is multi-session: RuntimeBackend.LLAMA_CPP exists (joulewise/schemas.py:184) but resolve_runtime has no branch for it (joulewise/adapters/__init__.py:147-150, verified).
feasibility: Mac/MLX today: strongest leg. Falcon-H1 hybrids have MLX-LM support and mlx-community 4-bit artifacts (Sol web memo, huggingface.co/mlx-community/Falcon-H1-3B-Instruct-4bit); Granite 4.0 hybrid (Mamba2/attention) MLX and GGUF artifacts exist per IBM/HF cards, though same-recipe conversion receipts are still needed; DeepSeek MLA support is in current MLX-LM releases (~8.8 GB 4-bit V2-Lite fits the 128 GB Mac easily); Qwen3-4B-4bit and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-4bit are already mirrored locally under /Users/edr/jw_models/mlx-community/. The state-spaces controlled trio is NEEDS-WEB + load-smoke: only mamba2-2.7b was confirmed in an mlx-community collection; generic mlx-lm loadability of transformerpp/mamba2attn under one pinned revision is unverified. 3080 Ti (12 GiB, D-073): JouleWise's only CUDA path today is the vLLM adapter over the node-worker protocol (joulewise/adapters/__init__.py:135-146) — no llama.cpp adapter exists despite the enum, so GGUF-based attention/hybrid subjects are not yet a campaign path on that node; DeepSeek-V2-Lite at 12 GiB is borderline (NEEDS-WEB/load verification). Sparse attention: no credible fleet path — Phi-3-small's documented block-sparse kernels target Triton/CUDA and actual sparse execution under local runtimes is NEEDS-WEB; a dense fallback must not be labeled a sparse-attention measurement. AMD/other: no adapter surface at all; out of scope per D-073 fleet posture. Same-artifact toggles: llama.cpp --flash-attn on|off is a genuine kernel A/B; --swa-full changes SWA cache allocation, not the mask; MLX-LM --max-kv-size is a rotating-cache policy, not a mechanism toggle; no MLA weight-absorption or SWA-mask-disable flag was established (NEEDS-WEB/source audit at the pinned revision).

risks: Family/tokenizer confounding is the dominant risk — no available attention pair is a true single-axis contrast, so every claim must stay named-pair L2 and gross-request-first per docs/contracts/token_normalization.md, and reviewers will probe exactly this. Quantization sensitivity may differ between SSM and attention layers, breaking 'same recipe' comparability. Runtime fallback kernels can silently make a 'hybrid' or 'sparse' subject execute a different path than its architecture label (worst case: dense-fallback measurements labeled sparse-attention). Cache-policy toggles masquerade as attention toggles (--swa-full, --max-kv-size). Output divergence at long context can fail C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY gates mid-campaign. The regression design invites the exact over-attribution the registry polices elsewhere (context-slope renamed attention-fraction). Fleet asymmetry: until a llama.cpp adapter lands, the whole axis is effectively Mac-only, weakening cross-target framing. Finally, this axis competes for the same quiet-Mac windows as the five already-committed D-070 axes, and Window A outranks everything.
